assertion.name: Differentiating Neuroblastoma Subtype
assertion.context: Diagnostic tumor tissue obtained before chemotherapy or irradiation
assertion.description: INPC subtype in which more than 5% of tumor cells have the appearance of differentiating neuroblasts, defined by synchronous nuclear and cytoplasmic differentiation: cytoplasmic and nuclear enlargement, a cytoplasmic diameter at least twice the nuclear diameter, and an eccentrically located nucleus with vesicular chromatin and a single prominent nucleolus. By differentiation grade, INPC places it in favorable histology when the patient is diagnosed younger than 5 years (up to 1824 days), provided the mitosis-karyorrhexis index also qualifies (see INPC Favorable Histology); from 5 years (1825 days) a favorable assignment requires further maturation beyond the neuroblastoma category. 422 of 4,680 Schwannian stroma-poor tumors (9.0%) classified at central review in the Children's Oncology Group Neuroblastoma Pathology Reference Laboratory between August 2001 and March 2012 were of this subtype.
assertion.notes: PMID:25207821 and the abstract of PMID:10421273 call this subtype "differentiated"; the INPC name, used in PMID:10421272 and PMID:41612478, is "differentiating".

selected_evidence.snippet: Tumors in this subtype are classified into the FH Group in patients diagnosed less than 5 years (1824 days) of age. To be qualified as having FH pNTs, patients over 5 years (1825 days) of age should have further tumor maturation towards GNB-i or GN (see below).

assertion.name: Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index
assertion.context: Primary or metastatic tumor tissue submitted before chemotherapy or irradiation, excluding bone-marrow metastases
assertion.description: An INPC morphologic indicator for tumors in the neuroblastoma category: the number of mitotic and karyorrhectic cells per 5,000 neuroblastoma cells, classed as low (under 100), intermediate (100 to 200) or high (over 200). At the Children's Oncology Group Neuroblastoma Pathology Reference Laboratory it is determined on primary or metastatic tumor samples submitted before chemotherapy or irradiation, excluding bone-marrow metastases. The prognostic meaning of low and intermediate MKI depends on age at diagnosis: among 4,282 neuroblastomas reviewed at that laboratory between August 2001 and March 2012, the INPC age cut-offs of 60 months for low MKI and 18 months for intermediate MKI were independently prognostic in multivariable analysis, whereas a 4-month cut-off within high MKI was not significant after adjustment, consistent with the INPC applying no age cut-off to high MKI. In a Children's Cancer Group series reported in 2001, MYCN-amplified neuroblastomas lacked neuroblastic differentiation regardless of patient age and were generally linked to increased mitotic and karyorrhectic activity, with higher MKI classes in younger patients.
assertion.notes: Left unbound. NCIT:C106317 Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index and its classes NCIT:C118955, NCIT:C118957 and NCIT:C118958 sit under Proliferative Index (NCIT:C28042), a Property or Attribute concept outside the HistopathologyFindingTerm enum, and NCIT:C163732 Increased Mitotic Activity covers mitotic activity only. The class boundaries follow the methods of PMID:25207821 and the review PMID:35053227 (high means over 200 per 5,000 cells, as in the NCIT:C118958 definition); the introduction of PMID:25207821 and the review PMID:41612478 write the high class as 200 or more, so a count of exactly 200 is classed inconsistently between sources.

selected_evidence.snippet: Histologically, MYCN-amplified tumors lacked neuroblastic differentiation regardless of the age of patients. MYCN amplification also was linked generally to increased mitotic and karyorrhectic activities. However, MKI classes in patients with MYCN-amplified tumors varied significantly, depending on the age at diagnosis, and younger patients had higher MKI classes.

assertion.name: Schwannian Stroma-Poor Neuroblastic Histology
assertion.context: Peripheral neuroblastic tumors classified by the INPC, whose prognostic grouping is designed for pediatric tumors
assertion.description: The defining histology of this entry under the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (INPC), which the International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee proposed in 1999 on the framework of the Shimada classification with minor modifications. INPC is an age-linked classification that depends on the differentiation grade of the neuroblasts, their cellular turnover index and the presence or absence of Schwannian stromal development. It places peripheral neuroblastic tumors in four categories: neuroblastoma (Schwannian stroma-poor), subtyped as undifferentiated, poorly differentiated or differentiating; ganglioneuroblastoma, intermixed (Schwannian stroma-rich); ganglioneuroma (Schwannian stroma-dominant); and ganglioneuroblastoma, nodular. Only the stroma-poor neuroblastoma category belongs to this entry. INPC was designed for prognostic distinction among pediatric peripheral neuroblastic tumors and is not applicable to adult ones, although there is no clear consensus on the age that separates the two groups.
assertion.notes: Left unbound. OLS searches of NCIT on 2026-10-20 for "stroma-poor" and "Schwannian stroma" (up to 15 results each) returned NCIT:C3270 Neuroblastoma, the Shimada classification terms NCIT:C85414 and NCIT:C85415, the composite tumor concepts NCIT:C42059 and NCIT:C42060, other neuroblastic tumor concepts, findings for other histologies (among them NCIT:C42049, NCIT:C42062, NCIT:C42063, NCIT:C42066, NCIT:C42068 and NCIT:C42071) and unrelated tumors and drug regimens, but no finding term for stroma-poor histology; searches for "Schwannian stroma absent" and "limited Schwannian stroma" returned no results. NCIT:C3270, whose definition includes the absence of a prominent Schwannian stroma, is this entry's own disease concept, and a bound histopathology term is exported as a has_phenotype edge from the disease.

selected_evidence.snippet: It should be noted that since INPC is designed for prognostic distinction among "pediatric" pNTs, it is not applicable to "adult" pNTs even though no clear consensus for separating these two age groups.

assertion.name: INPC Unfavorable Histology
assertion.context: Primary or metastatic tumor tissue obtained before chemotherapy or irradiation
assertion.description: The INPC unfavorable-histology group as defined for the neuroblastoma category: undifferentiated tumors and tumors with a high mitosis-karyorrhexis index at any age; poorly differentiated tumors, and tumors with an intermediate index, in patients aged 18 months to 5 years; and any neuroblastoma-category tumor in patients aged 5 years or older. The pre-treatment tissue rule and the differing use of the grouping by the Children's Oncology Group and INRG risk classifications apply as for favorable histology (see INPC Favorable Histology). In a Children's Cancer Group pathology review of tumors from the CCG-3881 and CCG-3891 studies, reported in 2001, this subgroup had 26.9% event-free survival. That figure belongs to its cohort and era: a 2022 review gives 5-year event-free survival of 54.6% for unfavorable and 88.1% for favorable histology (5-year overall survival 65.6% and 96.4%), citing the cohort analyzed for the 2021 revised Children's Oncology Group risk classification. In high-risk disease, histology after induction chemotherapy differs from the diagnostic histology, but the difference has not been shown to be prognostic: in paired diagnostic and post-induction resection samples from 94 high-risk patients on Children's Oncology Group trials (2001-2013), tumors resected after induction chemotherapy had shifted toward a more differentiated, less mitotically active histology, and neither histologic features at resection nor their change from diagnosis was significantly associated with progression-free or overall survival.
assertion.notes: Left unbound. NCIT:C85415 Unfavorable Shimada Classification sits under NCIT:C85413 Shimada Classification System, outside the HistopathologyFindingTerm enum, and its definition is written in the original Shimada terms rather than INPC's three named differentiation grades. No frequency is given because the share of unfavorable histology depends on the age and risk mix of the cohort.

selected_evidence.snippet: As mentioned above, the INPC offers the prognostic distinction between the FH group (5-year EFS+/-SE of 88.1+/-0.9; 5-year OS+/-SE of 96.4+/- 0.5) and UH group (5-year EFS+/-SE of 54.6+/-1.3; 5-year OS+/-SE of 65.6+/-1.3)

assertion.name: INPC Favorable Histology
assertion.context: Primary or metastatic tumor tissue obtained before chemotherapy or irradiation
assertion.description: The INPC favorable-histology group as defined for the neuroblastoma category: poorly differentiated or differentiating tumors with a low or intermediate mitosis-karyorrhexis index in patients younger than 18 months, and differentiating tumors with a low index in patients aged 18 months to 5 years. Among 630 neuroblastoma-category tumors in a Children's Cancer Group pathology review reported in 2001, this subgroup had 90.4% 5-year event-free survival. Under the INPC the grouping is to be determined only from primary or metastatic tumor tissue obtained before chemotherapy or irradiation, and once assigned it is not to be changed during the clinical course, because therapy-associated histologic changes may not have proven prognostic significance. The Children's Oncology Group and International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classifications use INPC histology differently: the Children's Oncology Group stratifies treatment using age together with histology classified by the age-linked INPC criteria, which by definition duplicates the prognostic contribution of age, whereas the INRG classification incorporates individual histologic features underlying INPC. A 2020 analysis of the INRG Data Commons recommended replacing INPC with those individual features in the Children's Oncology Group classification as well; that was a proposal, and when it was published the Children's Oncology Group classification still combined INPC histology with age.
assertion.notes: Left unbound. NCIT:C85414 Favorable Shimada Classification sits under NCIT:C85413 Shimada Classification System, outside the HistopathologyFindingTerm enum, and its definition is written in the original Shimada terms (differentiated or undifferentiated neuroblasts, stroma-rich tumors without a nodular pattern) rather than INPC's three named differentiation grades. NCIT:C177565 International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification Histologic Group is a qualifier under NCIT:C28076 Disease Grade Qualifier, also outside the enum. No frequency is given because the share of favorable histology depends on the age and risk mix of the cohort.

selected_evidence.snippet: Event-free survival of patients diagnosed between 1990 and 2002 (cohort 1; n = 10,104) and between 2003 and 2016 (cohort 2; n = 8,761) was analyzed. ... Replacing INPC with individual histologic features in the COG risk classification will eliminate confounding, facilitate international harmonization of risk classification, and provide a schema for more precise prognostication and refined therapeutic approaches.

assertion.name: Hepatocellular Degeneration
assertion.description: The liver is a confirmed cadmium target organ: postmortem and biopsy analysis shows gross cadmium excess in hepatic tissue, and human epidemiological data link cadmium exposure to hepatic fibrosis. Cadmium accumulates in hepatocytes bound to metallothionein, and when that binding capacity is overwhelmed free cadmium causes oxidative damage and cell death. Note that frank hepatocellular degeneration and necrosis is the expected consequence of that mechanism rather than a microscopic finding documented in the sources curated here — the human evidence in this entry establishes cadmium accumulation and fibrosis, not necrosis histology.

selected_evidence.snippet: Examination of the liver both in life and after death showed a gross excess of cadmium. This was also found in the kidneys after death.

assertion.name: Diffuse Alveolar Damage
assertion.description: Acute cadmium inhalation produces acute lung injury, and the lung is a confirmed target organ at autopsy in fatal poisoning. Diffuse alveolar damage is the expected histological correlate of the clinical acute respiratory distress syndrome, but the specific microscopic features often attributed to it here (hyaline membranes, alveolar edema, type II pneumocyte hyperplasia) are NOT documented in the sources curated for this entry; they are stated as the general ARDS pattern, not as an observed cadmium finding.
assertion.context: Acute cadmium inhalation

selected_evidence.snippet: Heavy metal inhalation is a rare cause of acute lung injury. Among the various heavy metals, cadmium is more commonly known to cause acute lung injury.

assertion.name: Renal Tubulointerstitial Disease and Fibrosis
assertion.description: The kidneys show proximal tubular cell necrosis with loss of brush border, tubulointerstitial inflammatory infiltrates, and progressive fibrosis. Cadmium accumulates in the renal cortex. Both cadmium and lead nephropathies are characterized by tubulointerstitial disease and fibrosis, though only early lead nephropathy shows nuclear inclusion bodies.

High-grade (BD3) budding is an established, stage-independent adverse prognostic factor now incorporated into the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classifications, and is associated with worse disease-free, overall, and cancer-specific survival in stage II-III colon adenocarcinoma.
assertion.notes: finding_term falls back to HP:0025461 because NCIT has no tumor-budding term in the Histopathology Result branch (searched 2026-08-17). The fallback is defensible here - budding is genuinely a cell-arrangement/morphology finding - but a targeted NCIT term request would be the better long-term fix.

selected_evidence.snippet: Tumour budding (TB) has been recognized as an additional prognostic factor in the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classification systems.

assertion.name: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (Immunoscore)
assertion.description: The type, density, and location of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes - in particular CD3+ and cytotoxic CD8+ T cells at the tumor core and invasive margin, quantified as the consensus Immunoscore - is a favorable, stage-independent prognostic marker in colon adenocarcinoma. A dense adaptive immune infiltrate predicts lower recurrence risk and is under evaluation to help guide adjuvant chemotherapy selection.
assertion.notes: finding_term is NCIT:C35983 Lymphocytic Infiltrate, "a morphologic finding referring to the presence of a cellular infiltrate that is composed of non-neoplastic or neoplastic lymphocytes in a tissue sample" - the closest match to the Immunoscore reading, which is a CD3+/CD8+ lymphocyte density. Candidates passed over (searched 2026-08-17, revised 2026-08-25): NCIT:C35980 Chronic Inflammatory Infiltrate is a morphologic finding but asserts a chronic-inflammatory character and admits lymphoplasmacytic cells and reactive plasma cells that the Immunoscore does not measure; NCIT:C12546 Tumor Infiltrating Lymphocyte is a cell type rather than a finding; NCIT:C160833 Tumor Infiltrating Lymphocyte Absent asserts the inverse of this finding; NCIT:C160832 and NCIT:C204678 are a CRF question and a count measurement rather than findings. The specific CD3+/CD8+ Immunoscore reading is carried by preferred_term and the description.

selected_evidence.snippet: the immunological data (the type, density, and location of immune cells within the tumor samples) were found to be a better predictor of patient survival than the histopathological methods currently used to stage colorectal cancer.

assertion.name: Low Proliferative Index
assertion.description: Adenomas show low mitotic activity and a low Ki67 labelling index. Most adult adrenal cortical carcinomas, by contrast, exceed 5 mitoses per 10 mm2 and 5% Ki67 — the proliferation-rate boundary is one of the most reproducible discriminators between the two entities.

selected_evidence.snippet: Most adult adrenal cortical carcinomas show > 5 mitoses per 10 mm2 and > 5% Ki67.

assertion.name: Circumscribed Lipid-Rich Cortical Adenoma
assertion.description: Grossly circumscribed, often golden-yellow tumour composed of bland lipid-laden cortical cells, without destructive capsular or vascular invasion. Cortical origin is confirmed immunohistochemically with SF-1, inhibin-alpha, Melan-A and calretinin.

selected_evidence.snippet: The pathological correlates of adrenal cortical proliferations include diffuse adrenal cortical hyperplasia, adrenal cortical nodular disease, adrenal cortical adenomas and adrenal cortical carcinomas.

assertion.name: Low Weiss Score
assertion.description: Adrenal cortical adenoma is distinguished from carcinoma by multiparameter histologic scoring. In Weiss's original series, none of the 24 tumours with two or fewer of the nine criteria metastasised or recurred, while almost all with four or more did. A Weiss score of 2 or less therefore supports adenoma. The 2022 WHO classification retains Weiss and modified Weiss alongside the reticulin algorithm, Lin-Weiss-Bisceglia and Helsinki systems.

selected_evidence.snippet: In addition to well-established Weiss and modified Weiss scoring systems, the new WHO classification also expands on the use of other multiparameter diagnostic algorithms (reticulin algorithm, Lin-Weiss-Bisceglia system, and Helsinki scoring system)

value.name: Nodular

ncit_mappings.mapping_justification: NCIT concept that MONDO records as an exact match of MONDO:0003325.

value.description: The INPC composite category: one or more macroscopic, usually hemorrhagic, Schwannian stroma-poor neuroblastomatous nodules coexist with an intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma component. The proportion of nodule to that component varies from case to case. The INPC also recognizes variants of this classical form. In one, neuroblastoma is found at a metastatic site while the primary tumor shows only intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma histology, as when a nodule in the primary was not sampled; in a CCG/COG series the unfavorable nodule was found only at the metastatic site in 6 patients even after complete pathology evaluation of the primary tumor. Very rarely, such a discordance reflects separate primary tumors presumed to be of different clones. Once classed entirely as unfavorable histology, nodular tumors are now divided into favorable and unfavorable subsets by applying the neuroblastoma criteria of age at diagnosis, grade of neuroblastic differentiation and mitosis-karyorrhexis index to the nodules. The nodular component is favorable when poorly differentiated or differentiating with a low or intermediate index in a patient younger than 18 months, or differentiating with a low index from 18 months to 5 years; it is unfavorable when undifferentiated or of high index at any age, poorly differentiated or of intermediate index from 18 months to 5 years, and of any grade or index from 5 years (60 months). Every nodular tumor diagnosed at 5 years or older is therefore in the unfavorable subset; in a CCG/COG series the favorable-subset patients were 4 months to 4 years 11 months old at diagnosis, more than half of them younger than 18 months. Umehara and colleagues defined the two subsets in 2000 from a review of 70 Children's Cancer Group patients. The International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee re-reviewed the same patients, confirmed the diagnosis in 67 and the survival difference (8-year event-free survival 86.1% in the favorable versus 32.2% in the unfavorable subset), and in 2003 proposed adding the split to the classification. An INRG analysis identified 232 patients with nodular ganglioneuroblastoma among 4,071 with a known INPC category; 83% were older than 18 months, 83% had unfavorable INPC histology and 2% had MYCN-amplified tumors. Outcome in that cohort was very heterogeneous, with event-free and overall survival of 54% and 68%, and in the unfavorable subset of a CCG/COG series 5-year event-free survival was 80.1% without and 16.7% with stage 4 disease. MONDO subdivides the class by background into MONDO:0004408 (stroma-rich) and MONDO:0004407 (stroma-dominant).

value.name: Intermixed

ncit_mappings.mapping_justification: NCIT concept that MONDO records as an exact match of MONDO:0003326.

value.description: The INPC Schwannian stroma-rich category: a transitional form between neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma in which a ganglioneuromatous component makes up more than half of the tumor around scattered microscopic neuroblastic nests, with no macroscopic nodule. It is always classified as favorable histology. Because the category excludes a macroscopic neuroblastomatous nodule, it is typically assigned on examination of the entire resected tumor, since intermixed and nodular ganglioneuroblastoma are hard to tell apart on limited samples (the diagnosis record gives how a biopsy diagnosis is reported). Most patients have localized disease: in a CCG/COG series, 2 of 189 patients with known INSS stage had stage 4 disease. In one referral series, biopsy and resection agreed in 17 of 19 patients with localized disease who had both, and the authors judged a biopsy adequate there, but a biopsy diagnosis of intermixed ganglioneuroblastoma made alongside metastases was not confirmed at resection in 8 of 12 patients, all given chemotherapy first, whose resected tumors showed neuroblastoma. Localized disease has an excellent outcome: in the CCG/COG series no patient with a favorable-histology tumor, intermixed tumors included, died of tumor, and in the referral series none of the 41 patients with locoregional disease relapsed. In that series 6 of the 12 patients with metastases at diagnosis relapsed and 2 died of disease.

assertion.name: Global neuronal loss with sparing of dentate nucleus and brainstem
assertion.description: Autopsy of individual I in PMID:34918187 showed severe atrophy of the neocortex, cerebral white matter and basal ganglia with massive neuronal dropout, while the brainstem, cerebellar dentate nucleus and the gross size of the cerebellum were preserved. The sparing pattern is the diagnostically informative part: this is not a uniform encephaloclastic process but a selective one that leaves specific structures intact, matching the imaging observation that brainstem and cerebellum look comparatively normal on MRI.
assertion.notes:
No finding_term is bound. The HistopathologyFindingTerm binding admits only NCIT terms reachable from the Histopathology Result branch (NCIT:C83490) plus a handful of HP rosette terms, and OAK searches of the NCIT Morphologic Finding branch on 2026-08-01 returned no term for neuronal loss or for a regional sparing pattern (candidates audited and rejected: NCIT:C50774 Tissue Degeneration and NCIT:C120874 Degeneration and Atrophy, both too generic to carry the sparing claim, which is the whole point of this record). The corresponding clinical phenotype is separately bound to HP:0002529 in the phenotypes section.
Neuropathology exists for exactly ONE of the five published individuals, so no frequency is asserted for any entry in this section.

assertion.name: Sarcomatoid Dedifferentiation
assertion.description: A rare high-grade component with loss of epithelial (keratin) marker expression arising within or after classic adamantinoma, sometimes with a completely "revertant" mesenchymal/sarcomatoid phenotype on recurrence.

selected_evidence.snippet: Three cases of adamantinomas with sarcomatoid transformation of the epithelial component have been described but the tumours still preserved an epithelial immunophenotype.

assertion.name: Tubular/Basaloid/Spindle-Cell/Squamoid Growth Patterns (Classic Adamantinoma)
assertion.description: Classic adamantinoma displays a spectrum of architectural growth patterns — tubular, basaloid, spindle-cell, and squamoid — within the same underlying epithelial-osteofibrous biphasic lesion. The keratin immunoreactivity pattern is conserved across all of these patterns, indicating a shared histogenesis; spindle and basaloid patterns are disproportionately associated with recurrence and metastasis.

selected_evidence.snippet: The most commonly associated patterns with recurrences and metastasis in a classic adamantinoma were spindle and basaloid.

assertion.name: Osteofibrous Dysplasia-Like Pattern
assertion.description: A fibro-osseous pattern resembling osteofibrous dysplasia, with only scattered or focal keratin/p40-positive epithelial cell clusters (sometimes detectable only by immunostain, not on light microscopy). Distinguishing an OFD-like adamantinoma from osteofibrous dysplasia proper, and from classic adamantinoma, is a recognized source of interobserver diagnostic disagreement (see `discussions`).

selected_evidence.snippet: one case with tumor clusters visible only on cytokeratin immunostain harbored no variants, whereas another case with tumor clusters visible on light microscopy and cytokeratin/p40 immunostains showed gains of chromosome 7, 8, 19, and 20
